values.DataCenterNotes: When Kinder Morgan launched the binding open season for this project in July 2024, its chief executive said the open season was part of meeting new gas demand for electric generation tied to artificial intelligence, cryptocurrency mining, data centers, and industrial reshoring. Data centers are one of several named drivers. No utility shipper or power plant fed by this expansion was found with its own data center tie.

verifications.note: A trade press article on the open season for South System Expansion 4. It quotes Kinder Morgan chief executive Kimberly Dang saying the open season is part of meeting new gas demand for power generation associated with artificial intelligence, crypto mining, data centers, and industrial reshoring.

records.researcher_notes: The tag rests on the developer's own statement at the start of the project, which names data centers among several demand drivers. It is about this project's open season, not company-wide talk. The named shippers are the Tennessee Valley Authority, Oglethorpe Power, Dominion Energy South Carolina, Southern Company Services, Atlanta Gas Light, and Santee Cooper. The Southern Company and Oglethorpe plants are not named. Dominion Energy South Carolina says 290,000 dekatherms a day of its share is meant for the Canadys Station gas plant, which it co-owns with Santee Cooper. Only critics, such as the Southern Environmental Law Center, and a speculative data center developer link Canadys to data center load. The utilities' own approval releases do not mention data centers, and the data center developer said in September 2026 that it is not tied to Canadys. So the plant link is not used. The August 2026 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approval article mentions data centers only in the opponents' arguments.

ledger.note: Tagged on the developer's own open season statement naming data centers among demand drivers for this project. The plant route was also checked. Shippers are the Tennessee Valley Authority, Oglethorpe Power, Dominion Energy South Carolina, Southern Company Services, Atlanta Gas Light, and Santee Cooper. Only Dominion Energy South Carolina ties capacity to a named plant, Canadys Station, and no utility or developer source ties Canadys to data center load, so the plant tie was not used.

Shippers are Duke Energy, 250,000 dekatherms a day, and the Public Service Company of North Carolina, 300,000 dekatherms a day, for the full capacity. The application says Duke needs the gas for forecast electricity demand and 8,400 megawatts of coal retirements. No Duke plant served by this project is named in the application, the project site, the trade press, or EQT's July 2026 earnings call. EQT's only data center remark was about West Virginia and the main line, not Southgate. Nothing found ties a plant on this project to data center load.

The shippers are National Grid utilities serving New York City and Long Island homes and businesses. No gas power plant or data center customer is named in the Williams groundbreaking release, the federal approval coverage, the New York approval coverage, or a Fortune article from April 2026. The Fortune article ties data centers to pipeline growth in general but not to this project. A Williams data center supply deal in the Northeast was found, but nothing links it to this project.

Phase III is two compressor units at existing stations, now due by May 2027, for Florida Power and Light and Duke Energy Florida. No plant is named for this phase. Duke Energy Florida's Citrus County plant gets Sabal Trail gas under older contracts and has no data center tie. Data center talk found is from advocacy groups about a newer, separate Sabal Trail expansion. No utility or developer source ties Phase III or a plant it serves to data center load.
